text: 2. CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT & COMMUNICATIONS 2.1. Website Updates In fiscal year 2025, the Solar Thermal webpages of Sandia National Laboratories’ Energy website recorded a total of 10,327 page views, with the highest traffic occurring in May (729 visits) and the lowest in February (148 visits). Notably, blog posts such as "CSP seminar series session focuses on bulk solids handling" and "Molten salt facility awarded $2.5M to restart testing" garnered 123 and 99 views and visits, respectively, highlighting the potential for targeted content to drive engagement. LinkedIn was the most significant social media platform. Articles shared on LinkedIn, such as "Molten Salt Test Facility Awarded $2.5M to restart testing," reached 14,358 members and achieved 379 link clicks, indicating a strong interest in relevant topics. Most visitors accessed the site from the United States, China, Germany, India, and the United Kingdom respectively, predominantly using desktop devices with Windows 10. Chrome, Bing, and DuckDuckGo were the most popular browsers. Traffic sources revealed that search engines were the primary driver of visits, accounting for 46.3% of total traffic, followed by direct traffic at 31.7%. The CST webpages underwent a major migration into sandia.gov between December 2024 and February 2025. In fiscal year 2026, our team will emphasize increased customer engagement and retention to engage more stakeholders, reduce the average bounce rate, and attract a broader audience. Figure 1. These tours play a crucial role in our outreach efforts, which allows us to share our work with a diverse audience both within Sandia and from various external organizations. Out of the 44 tours provided at the NSTTF, 20 were for Sandia employees, which included a special “NSTTF Intern Day” where we welcomed around 295 interns from across Sandia over the span of two days. This event allowed an opportunity for interns to gain insight into our operations at the NSTTF. Additionally, we offered several tours to internal Sandia partners. The remaining 24 tours catered to various external groups including UNM Leadership, multiple branches of the U.S. military, and congressional representatives from across New Mexico and the United States. 2.3.
